title: Complementary determinant polynomials multiply to the characteristic polynomial
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $T,P\in\operatorname{Mat}_J(A)$ for a finite set $J$, with $P^2=P$ and $TP=PT$. For the determinant polynomials [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly], $D(T,P)D(T,1-P)=\operatorname{charpoly}(T)$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module]. This includes an empty index set and the zero ring.

proof.text: Put p=C(P) and c=X1-C(T). Ring homomorphisms preserve p²=p, and scalar matrices commute with p, so cp=pc. Thus pcp=pc. Expanding gives (1-p+cp)(p+c(1-p))=c.
Apply Matrix.det_mul to this matrix identity. By the definition of Matrix.charpoly, det(c) is the characteristic polynomial of T. The polynomial on the complementary projection uses C(1-P)=1-C(P).
